q: Panchayati Raj institutions were given constitutional status by which Constitutional Amendment?
e: The 73rd Amendment Act, 1992 added Part IX on Panchayats to the Constitution.

q: National Panchayati Raj Day is observed every year on:
e: It marks 24 April 1993, the day the 73rd Amendment came into force.

q: Provisions relating to Panchayats are contained in which Part of the Constitution?
e: Part IX (Articles 243 to 243-O) deals with Panchayats; Part IX-A deals with Municipalities.

q: How many subjects are listed in the Eleventh Schedule for Panchayats?
e: The Eleventh Schedule, added by the 73rd Amendment, lists 29 subjects; the Twelfth Schedule for municipalities lists 18.

q: Which Article of the Directive Principles directs the State to organise village panchayats?
e: Article 40 asks the State to organise village panchayats as units of self-government.

q: Under Article 243, the Gram Sabha consists of:
o: Only the elected members of the Gram Panchayat
All persons registered in the electoral rolls of the village within the panchayat area
All residents above 21 years of age
e: Article 243(b) defines the Gram Sabha as the body of persons on the electoral roll of the village.

q: What is the minimum age to contest an election to a Panchayat?
e: Article 243F makes a person qualified if eligible for the State Legislature, but sets 21 years as the minimum age for Panchayats.

q: What is the normal term of a Panchayat under the Constitution?
e: Article 243E fixes a term of five years from the date of its first meeting.

q: If a Panchayat is dissolved before completing its term, fresh elections must be completed within:
e: Article 243E(3) requires elections within six months of dissolution.

q: Elections to Panchayats are conducted by the:
e: Article 243K vests superintendence of Panchayat elections in the State Election Commission.

q: The State Finance Commission that reviews the finances of Panchayats is constituted under which Article?
e: Article 243-I requires the Governor to constitute a Finance Commission every five years; Article 280 is for the Union Finance Commission.

q: The Constitution reserves not less than what proportion of seats in Panchayats for women?
e: Article 243D reserves at least one-third of seats (and chairperson posts) for women; states may provide more.

q: The Balwantrai Mehta Committee (1957) recommended a:
e: It recommended Gram Panchayat, Panchayat Samiti and Zila Parishad, called 'democratic decentralisation'.

q: Balwantrai Mehta, after whom the Panchayati Raj committee is named, later became:
o: The first Chief Minister of Gujarat
The Union Minister of Rural Development
The second Chief Minister of Gujarat
e: Balwantrai Mehta succeeded Dr. Jivraj Mehta as Gujarat's second Chief Minister in 1963.

q: Panchayati Raj was first inaugurated on 2 October 1959 at Nagaur, Rajasthan, by:
e: Prime Minister Nehru inaugurated the first Panchayati Raj system at Nagaur.

q: The Ashok Mehta Committee (1977) recommended a:
e: It proposed Zila Parishad at district level and Mandal Panchayat below it.

q: The PESA Act, 1996 extends the provisions of Part IX of the Constitution to:
o: Tribal areas under the Sixth Schedule
Scheduled Areas under the Fifth Schedule
e: The Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996 covers Fifth Schedule areas with special powers for Gram Sabhas.

q: Panchayats in Gujarat are at present governed by which law?
e: The Gujarat Panchayats Act, 1993 was enacted to bring the state law in line with the 73rd Amendment.

q: Who acts as the secretary of a Gram Panchayat in Gujarat?
e: The Talati-cum-Mantri keeps the records and works as secretary of the Gram Panchayat.

q: Who is the chief executive officer of a Jilla (District) Panchayat in Gujarat?
e: The DDO heads the administration of the Jilla Panchayat.

q: The administration of a Taluka Panchayat in Gujarat is headed by the:
e: The TDO is the executive head of the Taluka Panchayat; the Mamlatdar handles revenue work.

q: Gujarat's 'Samras Gram Panchayat' scheme gives incentives to villages that:
o: Elect their Gram Panchayat unanimously, without a contest
e: The Samras scheme rewards villages that choose their panchayat by consensus to promote harmony.

q: In Gujarat, the Upa-Sarpanch (Deputy Sarpanch) is elected by:
o: The members of the Gram Panchayat from among themselves
All voters of the village directly
e: The Sarpanch is directly elected, while the Upa-Sarpanch is chosen by the elected members.

q: Who presides over the meetings of a Gram Panchayat?
e: The Sarpanch is the elected head and presides over Gram Panchayat meetings.

q: The Constitution of India was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on:
e: It was adopted on 26 November 1949 and came fully into force on 26 January 1950.

q: The Right to Education was made a Fundamental Right under which Article?
e: The 86th Amendment, 2002 inserted Article 21A for free and compulsory education of children aged 6-14.

q: Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution on the recommendation of which committee?
e: The 42nd Amendment, 1976 added Article 51A following the Swaran Singh Committee's recommendation.

q: Which Article did Dr. B. R. Ambedkar call the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution?
e: Article 32 gives the right to move the Supreme Court for enforcement of Fundamental Rights.

q: The words 'Socialist' and 'Secular' were added to the Preamble by which Amendment?
e: The 42nd Amendment added 'Socialist', 'Secular' and 'Integrity' to the Preamble.

q: Under Article 243G, who endows Panchayats with powers and authority to function as institutions of self-government?
e: Article 243G says the Legislature of a State may, by law, endow Panchayats with such powers.
